lines.text: You Didn't Know Some Countries Printed Trillion-Dollar Banknotes.
What if I told you that you could be a trillionaire… and still struggle to buy groceries?
But that's exactly how bad things got in Zimbabwe.
In 2008, the country experienced extreme inflation.
Prices were rising so fast that money was losing its value almost every day.
And coming back later to find it costs hundreds, thousands, or even millions.
The situation became so extreme that Zimbabwe printed a banknote worth… 100 TRILLION DOLLARS!
That's a one followed by fourteen zeros.
Having a 100-trillion-dollar banknote didn't make you rich.
Because prices had risen so dramatically, that enormous number had very little purchasing power.
Eventually, Zimbabwe abandoned its collapsing currency in 2009.
A huge number on a banknote doesn't mean you're wealthy.
Because money isn't about how many zeros you have.
It's about what those zeros can actually buy.
You didn't know that about money.
